purpose: D188 golden-byte continuity manifest (round-39 finding 6). aggregate_algorithm: sha256( concat over vector ids in ascending Python string order of lowercase_hex( sha256( json.dumps(vector, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False).encode('utf-8') ) ) ) — over exactly the 127 vectors whose class is NOT one of the appended classes heads_listing_pagination / hpke-info-near-neighbors / abnf-schema-portability (the pre-D187/D188 set, listed under pre_fold.vector_ids). This is the formula that reproduces the value recorded at the D188 fold.
revision_neutral_aggregate_algorithm: the same aggregate after replacing the literal `rev <x-r402s-revision>` with `rev <REV>` inside each vector's serialization — only the seven `state-<machine>-edges` descriptions embed the revision stamp ("derived from state-machines.json rev N"), so this is the byte-continuity invariant that survives a revision bump with zero cryptographic change.
golden_revision_neutral_algorithm: sha256 of golden.json re-serialized (indent=1, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, trailing newline — the generator's own serialization) with the top-level `x-r402s-revision` member removed.

pre_fold.description: recorded at the D188 fold (round-38 fold 3/5, protocol rev 38): the committed artifacts at commit 9c5b13761 (before D187/D188; 146 vectors = the 127 + heads_listing_pagination) and at commit 38e7fe60c (after; 243 vectors) carry IDENTICAL values for every field below — the fold report's byte-identity claim, now reproducible.

current.description: the committed artifacts at protocol rev 40. Every difference from pre_fold is the revision stamp alone: golden.json differs from the pre-fold file ONLY in its `x-r402s-revision` member (38 -> 40); the 127 vectors differ ONLY in the seven `state-<machine>-edges` descriptions that spell `rev 40` instead of `rev 38` — the revision-neutral aggregates are byte-equal to pre_fold, which is the D188 "no golden byte changed" proof across the rev-38 -> rev-40 bumps.
